title: Grouse Grind Closed for Maintenance: What to Know

evidence.demandEvidence: Metro Vancouver's current parks advisory says the Grouse Grind is closed from October 13 to November 10 for annual maintenance work, creating immediate trip-planning demand for North Shore hikers.
evidence.readerImpact: North Shore hikers can avoid arriving for a closed trail, understand that the BCMC Route remains open but is a separate challenging option rather than a like-for-like easy detour, and plan transit and route-specific descent arrangements.
evidence.freshnessEvidence: Metro Vancouver's active park-alert page and Grouse Mountain Resort's current notice were rechecked on October 18, 2026, and confirm the Grouse Grind closure through November 10.
evidence.uniqueAngleEvidence: No existing Trends Today article covers the Grouse Grind or BCMC Route. The article combines the dated closure, the BCMC Route's open status, difficulty and dog rule, route-specific descent guidance, park status and direct transit access into one practical checklist.
evidence.cashProgressHypothesis: Measure article-level search impressions, clicks, engaged sessions, direct sessions and returning-reader sessions at 7 and 28 days. The repeat-use hypothesis is that a timely closure guide earns future visits for North Shore trail and park updates. App CTA clicks remain unavailable because no Farhaan app naturally serves this hiking task, so no app promotion will be forced. Ad revenue, sponsor inquiries, content cost and contribution remain unavailable until article-level attribution is exposed.

sourceCaptures.title: Park Alerts and Notices
excerpts: Grouse Grind Trail closed October 13 to November 10.
The Grouse Grind Trail will be closed for annual maintenance work starting Tuesday, October 13.
The BCMC Route remains open and offers a similar challenge, ending at the same destination as the Grouse Grind Trail.

sourceCaptures.title: Grouse Mountain Regional Park
excerpts: The Grouse Grind is 2.5 km one way with 800 m elevation gain and a challenging rating.
The BCMC Route is 2.9 km with 750 m elevation gain, a challenging rating and a more rustic trail surface.
Dogs are not allowed on the Grouse Grind or BCMC Route.
October 2 to October 15 park hours are 7:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

sourceCaptures.title: The Grouse Grind
excerpts: Hikers must purchase a Download Ticket for a Red Skyride or Blue Grouse Gondola trip down.
The first download for hikers is daily at 7:30 a.m.

sourceCaptures.title: 236 Grouse Mountain
excerpts: Route 236 runs from Lonsdale Quay to Grouse Mountain.
The Grouse Mountain terminus is stop 54290 at Skyride.
